genxml.title: VPro (Odyssey) PB&J display back end (publish-safe subset)
genxml.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
genxml.doc: Host-interface, I2C and scanout-buffer registers of the Odyssey board, and the header word that frames a display FIFO write.

struct.name: HIF_CTL
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Host-interface control of the display chip. The timing load puts the first clock-select field of the timing load in bits 14:12 and the second in bits 17:15 of the word read back from this register, then writes it twice: with bit 18 clear before the clock is programmed and with bit 18 set after a 100 ms wait. Start-up first writes 0x0006d3e0 (both selects 5, bit 18 set, low bits 0x3e0); that is a driver-written start value, not a reset value.

struct.name: ID
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Identification word. Bits 2:0 are the chip version the board information block reports. Bit 10 is tested at start-up: when it is clear, the driver probes the option port on the second I2C controller for a dual- channel display option, so a set bit 10 is read as "no option card" (inferred).

struct.name: I2C_OPT_CTL
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: I2C controller control register, option port (first of the port's two registers). The register-read routine reads it, clears bits 12, 8 and 10 of its shadow and writes it back as an immediate update. The driver reads this register at the first word of the read-back slot, not the second. Bit meanings are unknown.

struct.name: I2C_OPT_DATA
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: I2C controller status/data register, option port. The register-read routine polls it for bit 9, up to 133 times. Bit meanings are unknown.

struct.name: I2C_MAIN_CTL
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: I2C controller control register, main port (first of the port's two registers). The register-read routine reads it, clears bits 12, 8 and 10 of its shadow and writes it back as an immediate update. The driver reads this register at the first word of the read-back slot, not the second. Bit meanings are unknown.

struct.name: I2C_MAIN_DATA
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: I2C controller status/data register, main port. The register-read routine polls it for bit 9, up to 133 times. Bit meanings are unknown.

struct.name: FB_BASE_B
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Scanout base of the second buffer region, written by the frame-buffer set-up as a tile count shifted left 9, after rounding the region start up to a multiple of four. A tile is 16 by 16 pixels. Reading as a scanout base address is inferred.

struct.name: FB_BASE_A
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Scanout base of the first buffer region, same encoding as the second.

struct.name: SCAN_WIDTH
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Written 0 by the frame-buffer set-up, 0 or 1280 by start-up, and the timing load's active-width value (1280 in the built-in timings, twice that on one path) by the timing load. Active width in pixels is one reading; a pan offset fits the same writes (inferred).

struct.name: SCAN_HEIGHT
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Companion of the width register: 0, 1024 in the full-size form, or the timing load's active-height value. Active height in lines (inferred, same caveat).

struct.name: SCAN_CFG_A
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Written from the low two bits of a timing load value by the timing load. Meaning unknown.

struct.name: SCAN_CFG_B
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Listed among the addresses the kernel writes; no read of the source of its value was completed. Meaning unknown.

struct.name: SCAN_CFG_C
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Written from one flag bit of a timing load value by the timing load (the same flag as the colour-map unit configuration). Meaning unknown.

struct.name: FB_PITCH
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Scanout pitch: the frame-buffer width in 16-pixel tiles, rounded up to an even count. Reading as pitch is inferred from the arithmetic.

struct.name: FB_DEPTH
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Scanout pixel size code. The codes the set-up writes are 2 for 8 bits a pixel, 3 for 16 and 4 for 32 (established as values). The field width is not known; three bits is the least that holds them, so the field range is inferred.

struct.name: DCB_CTL
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc: Back-end interface configuration. The timing load stores a 3-bit timing load value here; its role is unknown (the field name is a placeholder). Start-up first writes 0 five times, which may be a reset or a flush of this register's function (unknown). Nothing reads it back.

struct.name: FIFO_HDR
struct.from: odsy binary analysis of the shipped display driver
struct.doc:
A write is a header word followed by COUNT data words that go to consecutive register addresses. The kernel normally sends the header and one data word together as one 64-bit store, header in the high half, and it pairs any two consecutive words into one doubleword wherever a header falls, so a decoder must treat the stream as a run of 32-bit words and not as aligned pairs. established.
The FIFO holds 24 doublewords (the driver waits until the level is at or below 24 minus the entries it needs). The level is a 7-bit field of a graphics-ASIC register. established. How deep the hardware really is: unknown.
Type. Only 3 and 7 are ever sent. Type 7 is used for the display-mode words, the cursor control word, X server colour-map loads and the cursor position when cursor control bit 2 is set; type 3 for everything the kernel loads at start-up or mode set and for the textport colour map. established as uses. So type 3 is read as apply at once and type 7 as apply at the next vertical blank, inferred from the pairing of uses. Bits 29:28 are set in both types and are probably a per-chip target select, one bit each for the two ASICs of a two-ASIC board (inferred from the name "all" in that driver). Bit 31 is never set. What the part does with a type nibble no software sends: unknown.
Read-back. Each register address has an eight-byte slot in the window; the value is in the second 32-bit word of the slot (the I2C routines read the first word; whether the board returns the value in both halves is unknown). The window returns what the FIFO last wrote at that address. A read does not wait for earlier FIFO writes (inferred); the driver reads only after the FIFO has drained.
